That Android setting can block the phone\'s replies to local devices. Check your VPN app\'s local network access and Android VPN settings. Linqavo uses the phone\'s default route; VPN coverage depends on that app\'s policy.

A device was approved, but its WireGuard tunnel has not completed a handshake. Check that both devices still share a local Wi-Fi or hotspot connection. If a VPN is active on the phone, check its local network access policy. Linqavo does not require a separate VPN or proxy.
Connect the phone to Wi-Fi, turn on its hotspot, or plug in a USB cable and turn on USB tethering, then try again.
A link is coming up but has no address yet — USB tethering can take a few seconds. Wait a moment and tap Try again.
Your PC cannot reach the phone over mobile data. Connect the phone to Wi-Fi, turn on its hotspot, or plug in a cable and turn on USB tethering.
Only the VPN tunnel has an address; your devices also need a local connection to this phone. Connect the phone to Wi-Fi, turn on its hotspot, or connect a USB cable with USB tethering enabled.
Another app is using the connection ports Linqavo needs. Close it, then try again.
This is usually battery optimisation, or Linqavo being swiped away from recent apps. Allow Linqavo to ignore battery optimisation from the banner on the home screen, then start sharing again.
The Wi‑Fi, hotspot or USB link this phone was sharing on went away and didn\'t come back. Check it, then start sharing again.
Linqavo\'s WireGuard endpoint couldn\'t start on this phone — usually a port another app is holding. Start sharing again; if it keeps failing, close other VPN or proxy apps and try once more.
Allow Linqavo to ignore battery optimization so sharing survives when the screen is off.
